$comment: FAMILY HUB SAFETY POLICY. The harness implements the rule KINDS; this file says
which of THIS product's calls they apply to, and with what vocabulary. Everything
here used to be hardcoded inside SafetyFilter, which is why the generic core knew
what a shopping list was.
grades.overrides may only make a grade STRICTER than the [SideEffect] attribute on
the method (A0 < A1 < A2 < AX). Loosening one throws at startup — see the ratchet in
SafetyPolicy.GradeFor. That is why this file can be edited without fear: the worst a
mistake here can do is demand MORE consent than the code intends.
Rules read constraints.hard and nothing else. Soft preferences never gate.

rules.$comment: Allergens/diet/medical. No module binding: a forbidden ingredient is forbidden wherever it appears.
Screen recipe RESULTS too, so a forbidden dish never reaches the model as a candidate. Recipes tag themselves with the same vocabulary (contains: [dairy, gluten]).

$comment: The budget guardrail: only the call that actually spends money.
DORMANT SINCE v7, ON PURPOSE. The household store no longer holds a budget_cap
entry, so no dispatch carries the key and this rule never fires in the demo. It
stays because a rule reads constraints.hard and does nothing when its key is
absent — there is no cost to keeping it — and because deleting it would leave
numeric_cap, one of the engine's five rule KINDS, with no instance anywhere and
therefore no coverage in gate 6. Seed a budget_cap and this works again
unchanged.
Quiet hours: things that make noise in the house.
Dormant since v7 for the same reason as the cap above — no quiet_hours entry in
the store. time_window_block still has a live instance (peak tariff, below), so
this one is redundancy rather than sole coverage; it is kept for symmetry with
the cap and because quiet hours are the first thing anyone re-seeds.
PEAK TARIFF (v6). The same rule KIND as quiet hours, pointed at a different
window — no new engine code, which is the point of kinds-vs-instances.
It binds only to Appliance, and only bites when the dispatch CARRIES peak_hours.
The cloud puts that key on energy_saving goals alone, so a guest dinner's 21:00
dishwasher run — inside the 17:00-21:00 peak window — is untouched. That is the
scoping doing its job: on an energy goal a peak-hour run defeats the goal's own
objective; on a dinner it is just how dinner works.
AWAY WINDOW (v6). Nobody is home, so nothing may be set running in the house —
an oven preheat, a dishwasher cycle, a defrost, or an announcement to an empty
kitchen. Endpoints are exclusive (see DateWindowBlockRule): the family is home
for part of the departure and return days, and 'run the dishwasher before you
leave' is the vacation plan's own best move.
This is the constraint that makes a vacation goal genuinely enforced rather than
merely advised — through v5 the away plan was pure suggestion.
